en: David Powlison tells this story.

text:
*슈퍼마켓*에 갔는데
그 엄마가 애를 데리고 왔는데
en: At the supermarket, a mother came in with her child.
The kid kept pushing her buttons:

text:
이거 사달라 저거 사달라
떼를 막 쓰고 난리를 치고
en: buy me this, buy me that, a full tantrum.
Watching, he got irritated.
Anger rose up.

text:
그 다음에 그 엄마가
너무 *화*가 나니까
en: Then the mother got so angry
she left the kid and walked off.

text:
그거는 또 *너무한* 거야
자기가 볼 때
en: That was too much, he thought.

text:
거기도 확 짜증나는 거야
또 *분노*가 일어났어
en: Irritated again. More anger.
"What's wrong with that mother?"

text:
두 가지 분노가 아닌
*또 다른 분노*가
en: Then a different anger,
not those two, grew in him.

text:
그것은 그 엄마가
왜 그렇게 애를 확 분노하고
en: Why did that mother blow up
and hit her child?

text:
그것은 그 *문제* 때문에
생긴 게 아닙니다
en: It wasn't about that moment.
In her life, piled layer on layer:
frustration, family troubles,

text:
더 깊은 삶의 깊은 *어려움*이
그의 삶에 이만큼 있는 거고
en: deeper hardships stacked this high,
and the child only set it off.
And why did the child act that way?
Maybe the parents divorced.
No father's love.

text:
뭔가 자라갔던
그 깊은 삶의 어떤 좌절과
en: the deep frustration of growing up like that,
that loneliness came out over one toy.
That could be it.

text:
그래서 데이비드 폴리슨 안에
생겼던 분노
en: So the anger that grew in Powlison

text:
이 두 사람을 이렇게 만든
그 *뒷세력*에 대한 분노죠
en: was anger at what made these two this way.
Why must we live like this?

text:
왜 이 땅은 이렇게 *고통받는*
사람들이 지내야 되냐는
en: Why must this world be full of suffering people?
Anger at the powers of evil.
And compassion for the people.

text:
긍휼과 분노가 함께 가면서
*정의*를 세워야 되잖아요
en: Compassion and anger together should set things right.
So what did he do about it?
A calling: "I have to become a counselor."
He saw it right there, in that store.
